# NavigationBar

The application's primary navigation: a bar along the bottom on a phone, a rail down the side from the rail threshold up.

## Anatomy

An optional brand block, shown only in the rail, then one button per destination with its icon over its label.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` *(required)* | `NavItem<T>[]` | — | — |
| `active` *(required)* | `T` | — | — |
| `label` *(required)* | `string` | — | — |
| `onselect` | `(value: T) => void` | — | — |
| `brand` | `Snippet` | — | Shown only in the rail, above the items — the reference's lockup and status line. |

## Variants

Bar and rail, chosen by viewport rather than by prop, exactly as the reference does it.

## States

Default and active per item.

## Keyboard

| Key | Behaviour |
| --- | --- |
| `Tab` | Moves through the destinations in order. |
| `Enter`, `Space` | Navigates. |

## ARIA

A `<nav>` named by `label`, with `aria-current="page"` on the active destination — the reference marks the active item by colour and weight alone.

## Accessibility acceptance criteria

- Reachable, operable and leavable by keyboard alone, with a focus indicator meeting 3:1 in both schemes.
- An accessible name for every control, and current state exposed programmatically.
- No meaning carried by colour alone.
- Legible and operable at a 360px viewport and at desktop width, and at 200% zoom.
- Interactive targets at least 44 × 44px on touch-capable viewports.
- The bar's bottom padding respects `env(safe-area-inset-bottom)`, so the last row of targets is not under the home indicator.

## Recorded deviations

| What | Why |
| --- | --- |
| `aria-current` was added. | The reference signals the active destination with colour and font-weight only. |
| The bar honours the safe-area inset. | The reference hard-codes 40px of bottom padding, which is its phone frame's home indicator rather than the device's. |
